papers.title: Deep Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Infrared-Thermography-Based CMT-Status Classification in Dairy Cows: A Comparative Evaluation in Egyptian Farms.
papers.abstract: Early and accurate identification of mastitis-associated inflammation is critical to increasing animal comfort, reducing financial losses, and enhancing milk quality. Although infrared thermography (IRT) has emerged as a viable non-invasive screening technique, the relative efficacy of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for automated CMT-status classification from thermal udder pictures is still unknown. This work carefully analyzed seven ImageNet-pretrained deep learning architectures using 976 thermal udder images (708 healthy and 268 mastitic images) from 48
papers.summary: This study compared seven ImageNet-pretrained deep learning architectures, including CNNs and Vision Transformers, for classifying California Mastitis Test (CMT) status in dairy cows using infrared thermal images of udders. Using 976 images from 48 cows on Egyptian farms, the authors evaluated model performance and applied explainable AI techniques to interpret predictions. The work provides a comparative benchmark for thermography-based mastitis screening, though the abstract is truncated and final performance results are not stated.

papers.title: Hierarchy-Aware AI Nuclear Phenotyping in Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes: A Preclinical Framework for Imaging Biomarker Development.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nuclear morphology and chromatin organisation provide quantifiable imaging features that may serve as candidate biomarkers of cellular state. However, many cellular imaging studies analyse multiple cells from the same microscopy field without explicitly accounting for their hierarchical dependence, which may lead to optimistic estimates of model performance. This study developed a hierarchy-aware AI framework to investigate DAPI-derived nuclear phenotypes in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). Methods: A six-day fluorescence microscopy dataset was processed usi
papers.summary: This study develops a hierarchy-aware AI framework for analyzing DAPI-stained nuclear morphology and chromatin organization in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, explicitly modeling the nested structure of cells within microscopy fields to avoid optimistic performance estimates. The work provides a preclinical framework for developing imaging biomarkers of cellular state from nuclear phenotypes.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion
papers.summary: The authors present AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework that uses a large language model to guide parallel multi-site sequence editing for simultaneously optimizing multiple therapeutic antibody properties. The method identifies promising edit sites and actions (substitution, insertion, deletion, or no change) to navigate the vast sequence space despite sparse annotations and property tradeoffs. This addresses a key bottleneck in antibody drug development where experimentally identified candidates require further optimization.

papers.title: [pMHCBind: predicting major histocompatibility complex class I-peptide interactions via protein large language models and hypergraph neural networks].
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules initiate CD8+ T cell immune responses by presenting antigenic peptides, a process fundamentally governed by the spatial interaction network mediated by multi-residue synergy between the binding groove and the peptide. Accurate modeling of this mechanism is crucial for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy. However, existing methods are largely confined to sequence-level modeling, failing to capture cross-residue higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained binding interface interactions. To address these ch
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The authors present pMHCBind, a computational method that combines protein large language models with hypergraph neural networks to predict whether peptides bind MHC class I molecules. The approach aims to capture higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained interface interactions that sequence-only models miss, with potential applications in tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy.

papers.title: Machine learning based predictive model for cardiovascular disease mortality risk in patients with stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.
papers.abstract: Patients with stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome are exposed to an elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality risk. However, large-sample, multidimensional prediction models for CVD mortality risk that integrate clinical indicators, as well as highly applicable supporting tools, remain lacking. A total of 2893 patients with stage 4 CKM were randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. The prediction model was constructed via variable screening using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator combined with multivariate Cox regression. Discrimi
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning-based predictive model for cardiovascular disease mortality in patients with stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, using LASSO and multivariate Cox regression on clinical indicators from 2,893 patients. The model was trained and validated on a 7:3 split, though the abstract does not report discrimination or calibration results. It addresses a gap in multidimensional risk prediction tools for this high-risk population.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study used 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 carefully designed sentences to test whether transformer-based language models represent sentence meaning like the human brain. By disentangling sentence structure from word meaning, the authors found that transformer representations poorly capture how word order shapes meaning representations in the brain, despite these models producing human-like language. The work suggests that current LLMs do not process linguistic meaning in a human-like way.

papers.title: BioHarness: Substrate-Aware Evidence Assembly for Biomedical Question Answering across Literature, Knowledge Bases, and Biological Atlases.
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assemble
papers.summary: BioHarness is a retrieval-augmented generation framework for biomedical question answering that dynamically decides whether to rely on retrieved literature, resolve gene and database identifiers, or query structured biological atlases for measurements. This substrate-aware orchestration aims to improve evidence assembly beyond fixed RAG workflows. The work is presented as a methodological contribution to LLM-based biomedical QA.

papers.title: Entropy Estimation: From Statistical Physics to Classification.
papers.abstract: Driven by the common entropy formalism in statistical physics and information theory, here we show that methods developed for the analysis of molecular configurational ensembles may be successfully used for classification. Entropy is estimated using the k-th nearest neighbor method combined with the Maximum Information Spanning Tree method to account for the mutual information between variables. This formalism is used to classify new samples using their estimated cross-entropy with the training set. The method is tested using the hand-written digits MNIST and the functional genomics CuMiDa dat
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that entropy estimation techniques from statistical physics can be adapted for classification tasks. By combining k-nearest neighbor entropy estimation with a Maximum Information Spanning Tree to capture mutual information between variables, the authors classify new samples via cross-entropy with training data. They validate the approach on MNIST digits and the CuMiDa functional genomics dataset.

papers.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Cid1 Poly(U) Polymerase: Catalysis, Substrate Recognition, Engineering, and Applications.
papers.abstract: RNA 3'-end modification is an important regulatory mechanism that influences RNA processing, stability, localization, function, and degradation. Beyond its biological roles, RNA 3'-end modification has become a valuable tool in biotechnology, enabling applications in RNA labelling, sequencing, engineering and oligonucleotide synthesis. Terminal nucleotidyltransferases are key enzymes responsible for template-independent nucleotide addition to RNA molecules. Among these enzymes, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase, has emerged as an important model for understanding RNA-specifi
papers.summary: This review examines Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase from fission yeast that adds uridine tails to RNA 3' ends without a template. It covers the enzyme's catalytic mechanism, how it recognizes its RNA substrates, efforts to engineer its specificity, and its use in biotechnology applications such as RNA labeling and sequencing. The paper positions Cid1 as a model system for understanding terminal nucleotidyltransferases more broadly.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Analysis Prioritizes YWHAB Within Ubiquitination-Related Transcriptional Programs in Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs may help characterize epithelial heterogeneity in endometrial carcinoma (EC). We aimed to identify candidates associated with these programs and epithelial plasticity.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics and single-cell data to identify ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs that characterize epithelial heterogeneity in endometrial carcinoma, prioritizing YWHAB as a candidate gene. The work links ubiquitination pathway activity to epithelial plasticity, suggesting YWHAB as a potential biomarker or target for further investigation in EC.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors present EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph features to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They build the model on PDBbind v2020.R1 and reduce homology-driven information leakage by clustering receptor and ligand sequences independently before splitting. The work targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across amyloid research, from predicting which protein sequences are likely to form amyloid fibrils to modeling their structures and designing inhibitors. It covers applications relevant to neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, framing ML as a transformative paradigm for the field.

papers.title: CPTAC Consensus Subtypes Add No Incremental Prognostic Value Beyond Stage and Grade in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Proteomic Reanalysis.
papers.abstract: Molecular subtypes from multi-omic profiling have refined the biological characterization of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but whether they add prognostic information to clinicopathological variables already in use is unclear. We evaluated the incremental prognostic value of proteomically assigned CPTAC consensus subtypes (NMF1-NMF3) against stage and grade, and asked whether subtype identity is carried by a biologically specific set of proteins. Subtypes were predicted from tumor proteomes in 211 patients under nested cross-validation and a locked hold-out design, and the analysis
papers.summary: This reanalysis of CPTAC proteomic data from 211 clear cell renal cell carcinoma patients tested whether proteomically defined molecular subtypes (NMF1-NMF3) improve prognosis prediction beyond standard stage and grade. The authors found that subtype assignment added no incremental prognostic value once stage and grade were accounted for, and they examined whether subtype identity is driven by a specific protein set. The work suggests molecular subtyping may not yet translate into clinical prognostic utility for ccRCC.

papers.title: Maternal Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Preeclampsia from Healthy Pregnancy but Not Early-Onset from Late-Onset Subtypes: A Leakage-Free Machine-Learning and Explainability Study.
papers.abstract: Early-onset (EOPE) and late-onset (LOPE) preeclampsia are clinically distinct, but their molecular differences are incompletely defined. Using a strictly leakage-free pipeline, we re-examined maternal plasma proteomes of EOPE, LOPE, and healthy pregnancy (HP) and asked whether the subtypes are separable at the proteome level. Label-free LC-MS/MS proteomes comprising 370 proteins from 46 women (HP, n = 18; EOPE, n = 17; LOPE, n = 11) were analysed using limma and fully nested cross-validation, in which feature selection, class balancing, and tuning were confined to the outer training folds; mod
papers.summary: This study analyzed maternal plasma proteomes from 46 women to test whether preeclampsia subtypes (early-onset vs. late-onset) can be distinguished at the protein level. Using a rigorously leakage-free machine-learning pipeline, they found that proteomic signatures clearly separate preeclampsia from healthy pregnancy but cannot reliably distinguish early-onset from late-onset preeclampsia. This suggests the two subtypes share a common plasma proteomic signature despite their clinical differences.

papers.title: Hidden Signals in Serum Protein Electrophoresis: Artificial Intelligence from Laboratory Pattern Recognition to Clinical Validation.
papers.abstract: Serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) remains a central laboratory method for the detection and characterization of monoclonal gammopathies and other dysproteinemic patterns. Despite substantial analytical automation, interpretation still relies largely on graphical representation and expert visual assessment, making low-amplitude or borderline abnormalities particularly challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) approaches, has increasingly been applied to SPE, with high performance reported for automated recognition of established abnormal
papers.summary: This review examines how AI and machine learning are being applied to serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) to detect monoclonal gammopathies and other dysproteinemias, particularly low-amplitude or borderline abnormalities that are hard to catch by eye. It traces the field from pattern recognition to clinical validation, highlighting reported high performance for automated detection of established abnormal patterns while noting the gap between laboratory performance and real-world clinical validation.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportuniti
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing use of Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy (Raman, IR, NIR, SERS) for tasks such as spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. It highlights how Transformer architectures capture long-range dependencies in spectral data and support applications across chemistry, biology, and materials science.

papers.title: PAZy: an expanded and actively maintained database of experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Plastics-Active Enzyme Database (PAZy) is a manually curated resource for enzymes experimentally shown to act on synthetic or bio-based plastics. It was developed to distinguish experimentally verified plastics-active enzymes from computationally predicted or insufficiently supported candidates. Here, we present an expanded version of PAZy, implemented as a relational database containing >450 plastics-active enzymes with more detailed metadata, broader substrate coverage, and large language model-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned web interface now enables browsing by prote
papers.summary: PAZy is a manually curated database of over 450 experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes, now expanded with richer metadata, broader substrate coverage, and LLM-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned relational database and web interface help researchers distinguish verified plastic-degrading enzymes from merely predicted candidates. This resource supports enzyme discovery and engineering for plastic recycling and bioremediation.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins—seven-transmembrane retinal-binding proteins found across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi—that mediate light-driven ion transport, light-gated conduction, and photosensory signaling. It traces the family's expansion since bacteriorhodopsin's 1971 discovery and discusses how channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics enabled millisecond-scale optical control of neurons, with particular emphasis on Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins as a basis for designing optogenetic silencing tools.

papers.title: The Construction and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Major Depressive Disorder Based on Astrocytes and Mitochondrial Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Astrocytes play an important role in depression. However, their specific mechanisms, especially their subcellular mechanisms, remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning model to classify major depressive disorder (MDD) using gene expression features related to astrocytes and mitochondrial dynamics. The model was trained and validated on public transcriptomic datasets, and key genes were identified that distinguish MDD from controls. The work suggests that astrocyte-mitochondria interactions may contribute to depression and that these features could serve as biomarkers.

papers.title: Label-Free Biochemical Characterization and Subtype Classification of Human Breast Pathologies Using Fingerprint Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for improved molecular characterization of breast pathologies. Raman spectroscopy (RS) provides a label-free, non-destructive approach for probing tissue biochemical composition. This study investigated Raman spectral alterations across five human breast histopathological categories and explored their potential for machine learning-assisted classification. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue specimens were obtained from five patients, with one patient representing each category: normal breast tis
papers.summary: This study used fingerprint Raman spectroscopy to probe biochemical differences among five human breast histopathological categories (from normal tissue to various breast pathologies) in FFPE specimens from five patients, one per category. Machine learning was then applied to the Raman spectra to classify the tissue subtypes. The work suggests label-free Raman spectroscopy combined with ML can distinguish breast pathologies, though the very small sample size limits generalizability.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Based Genomic Prioritization and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Growth Traits in Central Anatolian Merino Sheep.
papers.abstract: Growth traits are major economic drivers in sheep production, yet their genetic architecture is highly polygenic and influenced by multiple genetic and environmental factors. Here, we integrated machine-learning-based genomic prioritization and prediction with conventional mixed-model genome-wide association analysis to investigate growth traits in Central Anatolian Merino sheep. Phenotypic records for birth weight (BW), weaning weight (WW), six-month weight (W6), and average daily gains before (ADWG1) and after weaning (ADWG2) were obtained from 278 lambs genotyped using the Illumina OvineSNP
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study combined machine-learning-based genomic prioritization and prediction with conventional mixed-model genome-wide association analysis to dissect the genetic architecture of growth traits (birth weight, weaning weight, six-month weight, and pre- and post-weaning average daily gain) in 278 Central Anatolian Merino lambs genotyped with the Illumina OvineSNP array. The work demonstrates an integrated ML-plus-GWAS framework for identifying and prioritizing genomic variants underlying polygenic growth traits in sheep.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological prediction, and drug discovery. It argues that AI can overcome key limitations of traditional approaches, such as the slow and biosafety-risky culture of Brucella and the difficulty of distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains or natural infection from vaccine-induced immunity.

papers.title: Beyond prediction: The evolving role of artificial intelligence in genome editing.
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) system, genome-editing technologies have advanced rapidly, and the field has expanded substantially. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) has progressed at an unprecedented pace and is transforming genetic engineering. Early AI applications primarily addressed predictive tasks, including guide RNA (gRNA) activity, off-target effects, and editing outcomes for CRISPR-Cas nucleases, base editors, and prime editors. Recently, transformer-based protein language models (PLMs) and genera
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is moving beyond simply predicting CRISPR editing outcomes (such as guide RNA activity and off-target effects) toward actively designing and optimizing genome-editing tools. It highlights the growing role of transformer-based protein language models and generative approaches in engineering Cas proteins, base editors, and prime editors, signaling a shift from prediction to design in genetic engineering.

papers.title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to W
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to interpret and prioritize variants from whole-exome sequencing in neurodevelopmental disorders. It highlights that the bottleneck has shifted from variant detection to interpretation, and catalogs existing AI-assisted approaches for this task. The review is descriptive rather than presenting new data or methods.

papers.title: Prediction of Lindane-Induced Breast Cancer Toxicity Through Multi-Target Network Analysis and Mechanistic Investigation.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets associated with Lindane-induced molecular alterations in breast cancer and elucidate its toxicological mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. Lindane-related targets and breast cancer transcriptomic data were collected from public databases, and differentially expressed genes and WGCNA-derived hub genes were integrated to identify candidate targets. GO and KEGG analyses were performed to explore biological functions, while machine learning
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation to identify molecular targets through which the pesticide lindane may promote breast cancer. By combining lindane-related targets with breast cancer transcriptomic data and WGCNA hub genes, the authors pinpoint candidate targets and characterize their biological pathways. The work proposes a mechanistic link between lindane exposure and breast cancer-related molecular alterations.

papers.title: AIDCare: A Technical Proof-of-Concept for Integrating Personalized Nutrition, Physical Activity, and AI-Assisted Care in Diabetes Lifestyle Management.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical nutrition therapy and structured lifestyle self-management are fundamental to diabetes care, yet conventional mobile health tools typically track diet, physical activity, and glucose measurements in isolation, with limited connection to clinical oversight. This study presents AIDCare, an integrated mobile health platform that connects camera-based nutritional assessment, wearable physical activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and clinician-supervised conversational artificial intelligence (AI) to support personalized dietary and lifestyle self-management i
papers.summary: AIDCare is a proof-of-concept mobile health platform that combines camera-based food recognition, wearable activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and a clinician-supervised conversational AI to support personalized diabetes lifestyle management. The work demonstrates technical integration of these components rather than reporting clinical outcomes, positioning it as an early-stage prototype for connected diabetes care.

papers.title: Use of Demineralized Autologous Dentin Graft with the Tooth Processing Device in Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement and Loading: A 12-Month Evaluation of Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Stability.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of immediate implant placement and loading combined with autologous dentin grafting in reducing post-extraction tissue remodelling, with particular emphasis on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 13 patients (14 implant sites) with Type 1 extraction sockets in the anterior maxilla. Following atraumatic tooth extraction, implants were immediately placed and grafted with autologous dentin processed from the extracted tooth using the Tooth Transformer device. Screw-re
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated 13 patients (14 implant sites) who received immediate dental implants with autologous dentin grafts processed from their extracted teeth using a dedicated device. Over 12 months, the approach appeared to support peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone, suggesting autologous dentin may help reduce post-extraction tissue remodeling. The small sample and observational design limit the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title: FusionEP: Adaptive Cross-Modal Deep Fusion Network for Essential Protein Identification via Multi-Omics Integration and Contrastive Learning.
papers.abstract: Identifying essential proteins lays a foundation for dissecting disease mechanisms and mining therapeutic targets. Existing algorithms mostly adopt unimodal inputs and struggle to capture multi-level biological interactions from genomics, subcellular localization and proteomics. We present FusionEP, which is an adaptive cross-modal deep fusion network built upon contrastive learning to predict essential proteins. FusionEP integrates gene expression profiles, subcellular localization features, and protein interaction map structures. For gene expression information, we design a six-layer Transfo
papers.summary: FusionEP is a deep learning model that predicts essential proteins by combining gene expression, subcellular localization, and protein-protein interaction data through adaptive cross-modal fusion and contrastive learning. The authors claim this multi-omics approach outperforms existing unimodal methods, though the abstract is truncated and full benchmarking details are unavailable.

papers.title: Wavelet Scattering Features for Robust Subject-Independent EMG-Based Speech Recognition: A Comparative Analysis.
papers.abstract: Electromyography (EMG)-based speech recognition provides a non-acoustic alternative in high-noise environments and serves as a prospective foundation for assistive technologies for users with speech impairments. While prior work has largely focused on model architecture, the impact of EMG feature representations on the robustness and subject-independent generalization of deep learning models remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how feature representation influences subject-independent EMG speech recognition by comparing two feature extraction pipelines-a conventional Mel-Frequ
papers.summary: This study compares two feature extraction pipelines for EMG-based speech recognition, contrasting conventional Mel-frequency features with wavelet scattering features, to assess how representation choice affects subject-independent generalization. The authors find that feature representation meaningfully influences robustness and cross-subject performance, highlighting the importance of feature design beyond model architecture. The work supports non-acoustic speech interfaces for noisy environments and assistive use.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research.
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Ado
papers.summary: This review argues that artificial intelligence is shifting protein glycosylation research from prediction to generation, addressing three persistent bottlenecks: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of glycosylation occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. It surveys how AI methods are being applied to model and design glycans and glycoproteins, framing this as a paradigm change for the field.

papers.title: Construction and Evaluation of a Ketosis Prediction Model Based on Milk MIR Spectra and Feature Wavenumber Selection in Dairy Cows.
papers.abstract: Ketosis is a common metabolic disorder in dairy cows and occurs mainly during early lactation. Blood β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) is widely used for diagnosis, but large-scale testing is limited by sampling requirements and cost. We therefore studied lactating Holstein cows from 12 large-scale dairy farms in central China. Milk samples, milk composition traits, and milk mid-infrared (MIR) spectra were collected through the Dairy Herd Improvement (DHI) testing system from April 2019 to December 2022, and ketosis diagnoses were obtained from farm health records; samples were labeled as healthy or ket
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study developed a machine-learning model to predict ketosis in dairy cows using milk mid-infrared (MIR) spectra and selected feature wavenumbers, aiming to replace costly blood BHB testing. Using data from 12 large farms in central China, the authors combined MIR spectra with milk composition traits and farm health records to classify cows as healthy or ketotic. The work demonstrates that MIR-based prediction could enable low-cost, large-scale ketosis screening through existing DHI testing systems.

papers.title: Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Learning for miRNA-Drug Response Association Prediction Under Cold-Start Generalization.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Cancer drug resistance can be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which can alter gene expression and cellular pathways that determine how cancer cells respond to treatment. Potential miRNA-drug response associations can be identified using computational models; however, evaluating these models using edge-based evaluation can result in an optimistic view of model generalization since test miRNAs or drugs can appear in other response associations during training. (2) Methods: This paper presents a relation-aware heterogeneous learning framework that integrates miRNA expression pro
papers.summary: This paper introduces a relation-aware heterogeneous graph learning framework for predicting miRNA-drug response associations, addressing the cold-start problem where test miRNAs or drugs are entirely unseen during training. The authors argue that standard edge-based evaluation overestimates model generalization and propose a more rigorous cold-start evaluation setting. The method integrates miRNA expression profiles with heterogeneous graph structure to improve prediction of drug responses.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrated 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum depletion as a key microbial signature in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link these changes to hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling and suggest a therapeutic role for can (likely a probiotic or compound, though the abstract is truncated).

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines food-derived umami peptides as natural flavor enhancers that could reduce reliance on salt and conventional seasonings in alternative proteins and cultivated meat. It compares discovery approaches ranging from traditional sensory-guided preparation to modern virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization, emphasizing that practical value requires experimental validation beyond sequence prediction.

papers.title: Precision Cardio-Oncology: A Multimodal Approach to Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiovascular Toxicity Prediction and Assessment.
papers.abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) is associated with morbidity, mortality, and interruptions to cancer treatment. Current cardio-oncology clinical assessment tools generally rely on a limited range of clinical data; however, in the era of precision medicine, it may be possible to leverage multimodal data, including imaging and multi-omic inputs, to personalise CTR-CVT prediction and assessment. In this review, we examine the genotypic and phenotypic predictors of CTR-CVT and the evidence supporting their incorporation into multimodal risk models. Most research focuses on
papers.summary: This review examines how multimodal data—including imaging, genomics, and other multi-omic inputs—could improve prediction and assessment of cardiovascular toxicity caused by cancer therapy. It surveys genotypic and phenotypic predictors of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity and evaluates the evidence for incorporating them into multimodal risk models, noting that most current research remains focused on a limited set of clinical variables.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Identifies Putative Pathogenic HNF1B Missense Variants Associated with HNF1B-MODY.
papers.abstract: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 5 (MODY5 or HNF1B-MODY) is a rare form of diabetes caused by variants in HNF1B. Patients with MODY5 exhibit high blood sugar levels and symptoms commonly associated with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with kidney and pancreatic issues. Nonetheless, diagnosis, treatment and management approaches depend on specific genotype-phenotype associations. Interpretation of HNF1B missense variants remains challenging because of conflicting classifications and limited clinical evidence. This study aimed to improve the interpretation of HNF1B mis
papers.summary: This study applies an integrative bioinformatics pipeline combining AI/ML tools with traditional variant-effect predictors to reclassify HNF1B missense variants linked to MODY5 (HNF1B-MODY), a rare monogenic diabetes with kidney and pancreatic manifestations. By aggregating computational predictions, the authors identify a set of putative pathogenic variants that may help resolve conflicting classifications and improve genotype-phenotype interpretation. The work is a computational prioritization effort rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
papers.abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoni
papers.summary: ARGUS is an agentic framework that interprets noncoding single nucleotide variants by strictly separating deterministic biological computation (e.g., TF binding prediction, statistical evidence) from LLM-mediated reasoning, aiming to prevent hallucinations and fabricated experimental support common in LLM-only variant interpretation. It targets the >90% of GWAS variants in regulatory regions that remain functionally uninterpreted.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: The authors present LMEFold, a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). They then show that these predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting folding-initiation sites are functional hotspots. The work enables proteome-wide identification of EFRs that were previously limited by experimental and computational constraints.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Fight Against Antimicrobial Resistance: Applications in Diagnosis, Susceptibility Prediction, Precision Dosing, and Antibiotic Discovery.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, while conventional diagnostic, stewardship, dosing, and drug-development strategies remain limited by diagnostic delays, population-level decision-making, and a shrinking antibiotic pipeline. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help address these gaps by integrating complex clinical, microbiological, genomic, pharmacological, and chemical data.
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the antimicrobial resistance pipeline—from rapid diagnosis and antimicrobial susceptibility prediction to precision dosing and antibiotic discovery. It argues that AI can integrate heterogeneous clinical, microbiological, genomic, pharmacological, and chemical data to address gaps left by conventional diagnostic delays, population-level stewardship, and a shrinking antibiotic pipeline.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets serine/threonine phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders, enabling selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual targets including disordered substrates. This addresses a long-standing gap in chemical biology, since phosphatases are notoriously promiscuous and hard to direct to specific proteins. The peptide binders were designed using generative language models, suggesting a scalable route to programmable phosphatase targeting.

papers.title: Blood Cell Imaging Analysis for Multiple Sclerosis Classification Using Leave-One-Subject-Out Study with Deep Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease whose diagnosis typically relies on resource-intensive and partly invasive procedures such as MRI and spinal fluid analysis. This study explores whether deep learning can identify distinguishing patterns in RBC images associated with MS, aiming to determine whether blood-cell imaging may provide information relevant to understanding the disease. The initial dataset comprised 121 images from 13 independent subjects. To expand the dataset to 1944 images, image augmentation techniques were applied to the training data to increase image var
papers.summary: This study tested whether deep learning applied to red blood cell images could distinguish multiple sclerosis patients from controls, using a leave-one-subject-out cross-validation scheme to avoid data leakage. The dataset was very small (121 images from 13 subjects, augmented to 1944), and the work is exploratory in nature, aiming to see whether blood-cell morphology carries any MS-relevant signal. The abstract is truncated, so the reported performance and conclusions cannot be fully assessed.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals ACO2 as an Oxidative-Stress-Related Biomarker in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and memory impairment. Oxidative stress plays an important role in disease progression in AD. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying oxidative stress in AD remain unclear and reliable biomarkers for its detection have not been identified. In this study, bioinformatics analyses integrating differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to identify oxidative-stress-related differentially expressed genes. Using machine learning algorithms,
papers.summary: This study integrates differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analyses with machine learning to identify oxidative-stress-related genes in Alzheimer's disease, nominating ACO2 as a candidate biomarker. The work is a bioinformatics reanalysis of existing transcriptomic data without experimental validation reported in the abstract, so ACO2 remains a computational candidate rather than a confirmed biomarker.

papers.title: Growth Hormone-Related Gene Signatures Reveal Diagnostic Biomarkers, Immune Landscapes, and Potential Therapeutic Targets in Sepsis Through WGCNA and Machine Learning Analyses.
papers.abstract: Sepsis reshapes inflammatory, immune, and metabolic activity, yet the behavior of genes linked to growth hormone biology within this response has not been well defined. We therefore searched for growth hormone-related genes (GHRGs) that could distinguish sepsis and asked whether the resulting markers also reflected variation in host immune state.
papers.summary: This study used weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to identify growth hormone-related gene signatures that distinguish sepsis patients from controls. The resulting markers also captured variation in immune cell landscapes, and the authors propose candidate therapeutic targets. The work is exploratory and based on transcriptomic data, so the biomarkers require independent validation.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Deep Learning Integrating Multi-Regional MRI and Clinical Features for Predicting Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy: A Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Existing deep learning models for predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy often ignore the biological context beyond the tumor. This study aims to develop and validate a transformer-based model combining multi-regional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical data to improve BCR prediction after radical prostatectomy in prostate cancer (PCa).
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops a transformer-based deep learning model that integrates MRI features from multiple prostate regions (not just the tumor) with clinical data to predict biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy. The approach aims to improve on existing models that ignore the broader biological context surrounding the tumor.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and thematic review maps the landscape of machine learning applications in dementia research, covering diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. It highlights trends in biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches across the field.

papers.title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classif
papers.summary: This study empirically evaluates genome-aware weak-strong augmentation strategies for semi-supervised learning (FixMatch and FlexMatch) on DNA sequence classification, using a GROVER DNA language model backbone. It finds that augmentation designs tailored to biological constraints can yield more reliable gains than generic perturbations, though the abstract is truncated before reporting full results across the two classification tasks.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design through patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing traditional bottlenecks of long timelines, high costs, and inter-patient heterogeneity.

papers.title: Future of cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiac diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (cDMRI) has become a valuable noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis surveys the cDMRI literature to map publication trends, key contributors, and emerging research themes. It highlights the growth of cDMRI as a noninvasive tool for assessing cardiac microstructure and identifies future directions for the field.

papers.title: QAMQOR: a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition in robot-assisted autism therapy.
papers.abstract: Reliable engagement recognition is important for adaptive robot-assisted autism therapy (RAAT). However, progress remains constrained by the scarcity of publicly available benchmarks evaluated under realistic deployment conditions. Existing studies commonly adopt random train-test splits, which can inflate reported performance because recordings from the same child or therapy session may appear in both the training and test sets. To address this gap, we introduce QAMQOR, a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition collected during RAAT sessions with 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
papers.summary: The authors introduce QAMQOR, a new benchmark dataset for recognizing engagement in children with autism during robot-assisted therapy sessions. It includes data from 34 children and highlights that common random train-test splits can overestimate performance because recordings from the same child or session leak across sets. The dataset is designed to support more realistic evaluation of engagement-recognition models.

papers.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data using ensemble machine learning to identify isonicotinylation-related and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with in vitro validation of key findings. It highlights a potential role for protein post-translational modification and immune cell dysregulation in DMD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio and improved prognostication of renal cell carcinoma: machine learning-based analysis.
papers.abstract: To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC.
papers.summary: This study introduces the lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR) as a novel prognostic marker for renal cell carcinoma and uses machine learning to evaluate its added value over existing stratification tools. The authors report that incorporating LCR improves prognostic discrimination, suggesting a simple blood-based ratio can refine risk assessment in RCC.

papers.title: Taxifolin alleviates podocyte injury and macrophage chemotaxis associated with diabetic nephropathy by directly targeting RBP1 identified via multi-omics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Podocyte injury contributes to diabetic nephropathy (DN) progression. This study aimed to screen and validate the key functional proteins related to podocyte injury in DN, and to explore the protective effect of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine Linggui Zhugan (LGZG) formula against DN.
papers.summary: This study combined multi-omics and machine learning to identify RBP1 as a key protein in podocyte injury during diabetic nephropathy, then showed that the natural compound taxifolin (from a traditional Chinese medicine formula) binds RBP1 directly to reduce podocyte damage and macrophage chemotaxis. The work links a specific molecular target to a candidate therapeutic for DN.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approa
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys computational approaches for applying deep learning to EEG analysis, with a focus on diagnosing neurological diseases. It explains how deep learning enables automated feature learning to overcome challenges of EEG's non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability, improving diagnostic accuracy with minimal manual feature engineering. The review organizes the methodological landscape for EEG-based neurological disease diagnosis.

papers.title: Protective effects of testosterone replacement therapy on brain tumor outcomes: The Mayo Clinic experience.
papers.abstract: Biological sex and endocrine signaling influence cancer biology, immune response, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that testosterone signaling may exert brain-context-dependent protective effects in glioblastoma (GBM) through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression, and altered tumor-immune interactions. We assessed whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) exposure was associated with survival in solid tumor central nervous system (CNS) metastases and glioblastoma (GBM, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4), settings in which pos
papers.summary: This Mayo Clinic study examined whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is associated with survival outcomes in patients with glioblastoma and solid tumor CNS metastases. The authors report that TRT exposure may have protective effects on brain tumor outcomes, potentially through endocrine and immune mechanisms such as reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression. The findings suggest testosterone signaling could influence brain tumor biology in a context-dependent manner.

papers.title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether publicly available LLM chatbots can accurately organize and communicate the mixed evidence base on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI), including its heterogeneous phenotypes and evolving microbiome-related research. The work tests LLM utility as a tool for synthesizing uncertain, clinically immature evidence in a specialized immuno-oncology context.

papers.title: Natural language processing for suicidal behavior detection in short Spanish clinical notes from first-contact interviews.
papers.abstract: Suicide is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by social, cultural, biological, and psychological factors, whose early detection remains challenging. According to the World Health Organization, suicide is the third leading cause of death among individuals aged 15-29 years, representing a major public health concern for young populations worldwide. In first-contact clinical settings, screening opportunities are often constrained by limited time, sparse patient information, and operational workflows. This study evaluates the feasibility of detecting suicidal behavior from short Spanish-langua
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether natural language processing can detect suicidal behavior from short Spanish-language clinical notes collected during first-contact interviews. The work addresses a practical screening gap in time-constrained clinical settings where patient information is sparse, testing NLP feasibility for early suicide-risk identification in a non-English clinical context.

papers.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited.
papers.summary: The authors used a protein language model to design hemoglobin variants and then biophysically validated them, identifying a variant with improved stability and oxygen affinity. This work demonstrates that pLM-guided mutation prediction can be combined with experimental validation to engineer oxygen-carrying proteins, a step toward artificial blood substitutes.

papers.title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.
papers.summary: The paper introduces AIPFusion-Net, a computational framework for predicting anti-inflammatory peptides by fusing protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors. This fusion approach aims to improve prediction accuracy over existing methods, addressing the high cost of experimental identification. The work is a methodological contribution to peptide bioinformatics, likely of interest to specialists in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Characterization and clustering of immunocompetent proteins based on ESM-2 sequence embedding and physicochemical feature fusion.
papers.abstract: Traditional sequence-comparison methods face challenges when classifying and identifying low-homology proteins formed by convergent evolution. In this exploratory study, we built a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow combining high-dimensional embeddings from the frozen pre-trained protein-language model ESM-2 and weighted-fused physicochemical features. The workflow was explored for family-level grouping, identification of putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis of immune-active proteins. An independent external test dataset was further used to prelimi
papers.summary: The authors built an unsupervised clustering workflow that combines ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with physicochemical features to group immunocompetent proteins, including low-homology proteins that traditional sequence comparison struggles with. They applied it to family-level grouping, putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis, with preliminary validation on an external test set. The work is exploratory and demonstrates a proof-of-concept rather than a validated classification method.
